The Role of Technology Accessibility in Social Connectedness and Health-Related Quality of Life for Rural Older Adults
papers.abstract: Objectives This study aims to examine the relationship between social connectedness and health-related quality of life (HRQoL) among older adults, focusing on the impact of technology accessibility and geographic context (urban vs. rural). Methods Data from the 2021 National Health and Aging Trends Study (NHATS) with 2303 participants aged 65 and older were used. Confirmatory factor analysis validated measures of social connectedness and HRQoL, followed by regression analysis to explore their relationship, including the moderating roles of technology accessibility and geographic context. Results The findings indicate a significant positive relationship between social connectedness and HRQoL. However, technology accessibility moderates this relationship only in rural areas, where lower technology access enhances the positive effects of social connectedness on HRQoL. Discussion The results suggest that interventions to improve HRQoL among older adults should consider different geographical locations. Notably, promoting in-person interactions is crucial for enhancing the HRQoL of rural older adults.
papers.tldr: The findings indicate a significant positive relationship between social connectedness and HRQoL, however, technology accessibility moderates this relationship only in rural areas, where lower technology access enhances the positive effects of social connectedness on HRQoL.

papers.title: Advancements in Hand Gesture Technology for Enhancing Accessibility in Disability Assistance
papers.abstract: Hand gesture recognition technology has become a crucial innovation in assistive technology, providing enhanced accessibility and independence for individuals with disabilities. In order to enhance communication, mobility, and rehabilitation support, this paper investigates the development and integration of AI-powered gesture recognition systems with wearable devices, augmented reality (AR), and the Internet of Things (IoT). The adaptability and ease of use of the current solutions, such as sign language interpretation and smart prosthetics, are severely limited. We propose a novel framework that combines cloud-based data storage, haptic feedback mechanisms, and real-time AI processing to create a highly responsive and personalized user experience to fill in these gaps. The research focuses on accuracy, responsiveness, and ease of use during its comprehensive analysis of prototype testing data and user feedback. The system is able to continually improve the accuracy of gesture recognition and adapt to the requirements of each user by making use of deep learning algorithms. The study also emphasizes the possibility of incorporating brain-computer interfaces (BCIs) for improved control and responsiveness. By providing individualized therapeutic exercises and real-time feedback, our findings suggest that incorporating gesture-controlled interfaces into rehabilitation programs can significantly benefit stroke patients and individuals with motor impairments. Gesture-based smart home control is also made possible by IoT connectivity, which makes life easier for people with limited mobility. An assessment of the system’s impact, obstacles to widespread adoption, and potential future directions for improving AI models and making them more affordable are presented at the study’s conclusion. The goal of this study is to help close the digital divide for people with disabilities and contribute to the ongoing development of accessible technology.
papers.venue: 2025 2nd International Conference on New Frontiers in Communication, Automation, Management and Security (ICCAMS)

papers.title: Diabetes Technology Accessibility in Deaf and Hard of Hearing People With Diabetes
papers.abstract: Deaf and hard of hearing (DHH) populations face higher rates of diabetes and systemic barriers accessing diabetes technology. Effective use of diabetes technology relies on sensory (e.g., visual and audible) input and interpretation by the user. This study evaluates the accessibility of continuous glucose monitoring systems (CGMs) and insulin pumps for DHH individuals.
papers.tldr: This study evaluates the accessibility of continuous glucose monitoring systems (CGMs) and insulin pumps for DHH individuals.

papers.title: VRSight: An AI-Driven Scene Description System to Improve Virtual Reality Accessibility for Blind People
papers.abstract: Virtual Reality (VR) is inaccessible to blind people. While research has investigated many techniques to enhance VR accessibility, they require additional developer effort to integrate. As such, most mainstream VR apps remain inaccessible as the industry de-prioritizes accessibility. We present VRSight, an end-to-end system that recognizes VR scenes post hoc through a set of AI models (e.g., object detection, depth estimation, LLM-based atmosphere interpretation) and generates tone-based, spatial audio feedback, empowering blind users to interact in VR without developer intervention. To enable virtual element detection, we further contribute DISCOVR, a VR dataset consisting of 30 virtual object classes from 17 social VR apps, substituting real-world datasets that remain not applicable to VR contexts. Nine participants used VRSight to explore an off-the-shelf VR app (Rec Room), demonstrating its effectiveness in facilitating social tasks like avatar awareness and available seat identification.
papers.tldr: VRSight is presented, an end-to-end system that recognizes VR scenes post hoc through a set of AI models and generates tone-based, spatial audio feedback, empowering blind users to interact in VR without developer intervention.
papers.venue: ACM Symposium on User Interface Software and Technology

papers.title: Visual design and accessibility settings: an exploratory study on their role in technology adoption among older adults
papers.abstract: Mobile navigation is often perceived as simple and intuitive due to the apparent ease with which users can perform complex tasks. However, it remains a significant source of frustration for older adults, representing a substantial barrier to the adoption and appropriation of digital technologies. This study focuses on users aged 65 and older, a group that faces specific challenges such as difficulty performing certain gestures and interpreting the meaning of icons, with the visual style in which these are rendered being the most important factor. The research explores whether older adults are aware of and use accessibility settings, and to what extent these features enhance their user experience. Data were collected through two focus groups with participants aged 65 and older, with particular attention paid to their understanding of graphical user interface iconography in mobile apps and their ability to configure accessibility options. Findings reveal that activating accessibility features can, in some cases, negatively impact usability and user experience by altering the original visual design of the application. Moreover, many older users struggle to independently configure these settings. The study highlights the pivotal role of family members and close contacts as “warm experts” who assist older adults in the process of technology adoption.
papers.tldr: Findings reveal that activating accessibility features can, in some cases, negatively impact usability and user experience by altering the original visual design of the application.

papers.title: A11yExtensions: Accessibility Extensions to Augment Mobile AI Assistive Technology In-Situ
papers.abstract: Existing visual AI assistive technologies have usability gaps, and may need additional adaptations and features to serve users’ needs. We propose A11yExtensions, in-situ interventions that augment existing mobile AI assistive technology with add-on services. Add-ons include features that have been researched but are not yet deployed (e.g., cross-checking AI results), or that are only available in certain applications (e.g., camera aiming assistance). Through co-design sessions with two blind accessibility professionals, we designed and implemented three exemplar extensions, leveraging mobile automation tools to invoke add-ons, enabling just-in-time interventions for adaptability. We found that A11yExtensions provide opportunities to test new features and a new degree of flexibility and customization, though they introduce additional onboarding and communication challenges. We also derived a design space of accessibility extensions as a basis for future extension designs. Overall, A11yExtensions is a demonstration of the effectiveness of deploying new features in-situ via automation, with the technologies people actually use in their day-to-day lives.
papers.tldr: A11yExtensions, in-situ interventions that augment existing mobile AI assistive technology with add-on services, is a demonstration of the effectiveness of deploying new features in-situ via automation, with the technologies people actually use in their day-to-day lives.
papers.venue: International Conference on Human Factors in Computing Systems

papers.title: Improving Web Accessibility With an LLM-Based Tool: A Preliminary Evaluation for STEM Images
papers.abstract: Ensuring equitable access to web-based visual content in Science, Technology, Engineering, and Mathematics (STEM) disciplines remains a significant challenge for visually impaired users. This preliminary study explores the use of Large Language Models (LLMs) to automatically generate high-quality alternative texts for complex web images in these domains, contributing to the development of an accessibility tool. First, we analyzed the outputs of various LLM-based image-captioning systems, selected the most suitable one (Gemini), and developed a browser extension, AlternAtIve, capable of generating alternative descriptions at varying verbosity levels. To evaluate AlternAtIve, we assessed its perceived usefulness in a study involving 35 participants, including a blind user. Additionally, we manually compared the quality of the outputs generated by AlternAtIve with those provided by two state-of-the-practice tools from the Google Web Store, using a custom metric that computes the quality of the descriptions considering their correctness, usefulness, and completeness. The results show that the descriptions generated with AlternAtIve achieved high quality scores, almost always better than those of the other two tools. Although conveying the meaning of complex images to visually impaired users through descriptions remains challenging, the findings suggest that AI-based tools, such as AlternAtIve, can significantly improve the web navigation experience for screen reader users.
papers.tldr: Although conveying the meaning of complex images to visually impaired users through descriptions remains challenging, the findings suggest that AI-based tools, such as AlternAtIve, can significantly improve the web navigation experience for screen reader users.

papers.title: Between Regulation and Accessibility: How Chinese University Students Navigate Global and Domestic Generative AI
papers.abstract: Despite the rapid proliferation of generative AI in higher education, students in China face significant barriers in accessing global tools like ChatGPT due to regulations and constraints. Grounded in the Unified Theory of Acceptance and Use of Technology 2 (UTAUT2) model, this study employs qualitative interviews to investigate how Chinese university students interact with both global and domestic generative AIs in the learning process. Findings reveal that engagement is shaped by accessibility, language proficiency, and cultural relevance. Students often employ workarounds (e.g., VPNs) to access global generative AIs, raising ethical and privacy concerns. Domestic generative AIs, while offering language and cultural advantages, are limited by content filtering and output constraints. This research contributes to understanding generative AI adoption in non-Western contexts by highlighting the complex interplay of political, linguistic, and cultural factors. It advocates for human-centered, multilingual, domestic context-sensitive AI integration to ensure equitable and inclusive digital learning environments.
papers.tldr: Investigation of how Chinese university students interact with both global and domestic generative AIs in the learning process reveals that engagement is shaped by accessibility, language proficiency, and cultural relevance.

papers.title: Facing Challenges in Higher Education: Enhancing Accessibility and Inclusion Through Flexible Learning Design
papers.abstract: The increasing cultural and demographic diversity among higher education students highlights the challenges regarding accessibility and inclusion. The COVID-19 pandemic has accelerated the shift toward flexible, technology-based teaching practices. However, inclusive, and accessible pedagogical practices lack consistency, particularly when supporting students with disabilities or diverse learning needs. This study evaluates the effectiveness of the Learning Design for Flexible Education (FLeD) Tool—a web-based platform developed to support teachers in designing flexible and inclusive learning scenarios. The research adopts a qualitative approach, featuring semi-structured interviews with two Portuguese experts in accessibility and inclusion. The experts analyzed three learning scenarios designed using the FLeD Tool, through the lens of Universal Design for Learning standards. The collected dataset was analyzed using thematic analysis to identify common issues, strengths, and opportunities for improvement. The findings show a gap between institutional policies and their practical application, mainly due to inconsistent teacher training and technical limitations. While the FLeD Tool supports more flexible and inclusive pedagogical designs, experts have identified key shortcomings such as the lack of automated accessibility checks and limited support for specific disabilities. Despite the reduced number of participants (two experts) and dataset (three learning scenarios), which limits the study’s generalizability, the conclusions draw attention to the pivotal role of systematic teacher training, embedded accessibility features and solid institutional policies in bridging the gap between policy aspiration and effective inclusive practice.
papers.tldr: The findings show a gap between institutional policies and their practical application, mainly due to inconsistent teacher training and technical limitations, and draw attention to the pivotal role of systematic teacher training, embedded accessibility features and solid institutional policies in bridging the gap between policy aspiration and effective inclusive practice.

papers.title: Examining the Influence of Technological Perception, Cost, and Accessibility on Electric Vehicle Consumer Behavior in Thailand
papers.abstract: This study investigates consumer behavior in electric vehicle (EV) adoption, focusing on how factors like convenience, accessibility, technological perception, and cost influence the travel patterns and usage behavior of EV drivers in Thailand. This study aims to address the research gap in the comparative behavior between electric vehicles and public transport in a developing country. Using a quantitative approach, the study collected data via surveys distributed online and face-to-face interviews with a stratified sample of 398 respondents. The survey assessed the relationships between convenience and accessibility, technology perception, cost of ownership, and travel patterns using structural equation modeling (SEM). The findings reveal that convenience and accessibility significantly affect consumer perceptions of technology and the cost of ownership, which, in turn, influences travel patterns. Technology perception and performance serve as partial mediators, suggesting that improving the infrastructure enhances EV adoption. Additionally, the cost of ownership, including long-term savings, positively impacts usage behavior. This study provides key insights for policymakers and urban planners aiming to promote the adoption of EVs. Enhancing charging infrastructure, offering government incentives, and improving public awareness of long-term cost benefits are recommended strategies. These findings are particularly relevant in urban environments and offer guidance for developing infrastructure policies that align with consumer preferences.

papers.title: Modeling Accessibility: Characterizing What We Mean by “Accessible”
papers.abstract: Accessibility research has a broad mandate: use technology to make the world more accessible to disabled people. Yet, as a field, accessibility research lacks a clear characterization of what “accessibility” is. Furthermore, it has been historically limited in who is designed for, focusing on specific types of disability and often failing to consider how disability intersects with other identities. We set out to explicate what it means to make something accessible, grounded in the lived experiences of a diverse group of 25 disabled people. From our empirical findings, we develop a process for modeling accessibility. First, an individual assesses their experience of inaccess, specifically, the type of barrier they face, the technology repertoire they possess, and the contextual factors that shape how they address accessibility barriers. Then, having assessed an access barrier, they perform consequence calculus, weighing all available options to achieve access and deciding upon the option that best matches their priorities. We highlight the situated nature of access; people’s identities, contextual factors, repertoires, and priorities all dictate their experience of accessibility.
papers.venue: International ACM SIGACCESS Conference on Computers and Accessibility

papers.title: Accessibility Scout: Personalized Accessibility Scans of Built Environments
papers.abstract: Assessing the accessibility of unfamiliar built environments is critical for people with disabilities. However, manual assessments, performed by users or their personal health professionals, are laborious and unscalable, while automatic machine learning methods often neglect an individual user’s unique needs. Recent advances in Large Language Models (LLMs) enable novel approaches to this problem, balancing personalization with scalability to enable more adaptive and context-aware assessments of accessibility. We present Accessibility Scout, an LLM-based accessibility scanning system that identifies accessibility concerns from photos of built environments. With use, Accessibility Scout becomes an increasingly capable "accessibility scout", tailoring accessibility scans to an individual’s mobility level, preferences, and specific environmental interests through collaborative Human-AI assessments. We present findings from three studies: a formative study with six participants to inform the design of Accessibility Scout, a technical evaluation of 500 images of built environments, and a user study with 10 participants of varying mobility. Results from our technical evaluation and user study show that Accessibility Scout can generate personalized accessibility scans that extend beyond traditional ADA considerations. Finally, we conclude with a discussion on the implications of our work and future steps for building more scalable and personalized accessibility assessments of the physical world.
papers.tldr: Results from the technical evaluation and user study show that Accessibility Scout can generate personalized accessibility scans that extend beyond traditional ADA considerations, and this work presents Accessibility Scout, an LLM-based accessibility scanning system that identifies accessibility concerns from photos of built environments.
papers.venue: ACM Symposium on User Interface Software and Technology

papers.title: Deep Learning-Driven Geospatial Modeling of Elderly Care Accessibility: Disparities Across the Urban-Rural Continuum in Central China
papers.abstract: With the intensification of aging, the imbalance between the supply and demand of elderly care services has become increasingly prominent. Taking Changsha as a case study, this research constructs an accessibility evaluation system based on the 15-min life circle theory, utilizing multi-source data. Spatial weighting characteristics of elderly care facility locations were analyzed through machine learning algorithms, and service coverage disparities between urban districts and suburban towns were assessed under 5-, 10-, and 15-min walking thresholds. Street view semantic segmentation technology was employed to extract street environmental elements in central urban areas, and a multiple regression model was established to elucidate the impact mechanisms of the built environment on walking accessibility. Key findings include: (1) Significant urban-rural service disparities exist, with 91.4% of urban core facilities offering seven service categories within 15-min walking catchments compared to 26.86% in township areas, demonstrating suburban infrastructure’s heavy reliance on administrative resource allocation. (2) Street environmental factors exhibit significant correlations with walking accessibility scores. At the 15-min walking threshold, building space ratio and transportation infrastructure coverage positively influenced walking convenience, while sky view ratio showed a negative correlation. (3) A random forest-based location prediction framework identified multiple service gaps in existing facilities. Suburban service deficiencies (e.g., 59.8% medical facility coverage within walkable catchments) emerge as critical equity barriers, prompting recommendations for integrated “micro-clinic + smart pharmacy” networks and prioritized mixed-use zoning in new urban planning. This research advances a data-driven framework for reconciling urbanization-aging conflicts, offering practical insights for developing nations in creating age-friendly urban environments.
papers.tldr: This research constructs an accessibility evaluation system based on the 15-min life circle theory, offering practical insights for developing nations in creating age-friendly urban environments through data-driven framework for reconciling urbanization-aging conflicts.

papers.title: Aromatic polyketides from the marine-derived fungus Aspergillus unguis PM03: α-glucosidase inhibitory activity, structure-activity relationship, molecular docking and ADMET evaluation
papers.abstract: Chemical investigation of Aspergillus unguis PM03 yielded eight known aromatic polyketides, including unguinol (1), nidulin (2), 2,4-dichlorounguinol (3), 2-chlorounguinol (4), emeguisin B (5), aspergillusether A (6), guisinol (7), and isosclerone (8). Their structures were established by spectroscopic analysis and comparison with published data. All isolated compounds were evaluated for cytotoxicity against four human cancer cell lines (KB, Hep-G2, A549, and MCF-7) and for α-glucosidase inhibitory activity. None of the compounds exhibited significant cytotoxicity (IC50 > 128 μM). Compounds 1, 3, 5, 7, and 8 inhibited α-glucosidase, with guisinol (7) showing the strongest activity (IC50 = 4.01 μM), followed by isosclerone (8) (11.39 μM), emeguisin B (5) (24.31 μM), unguinol (1) (26.28 μM), and 2,4-dichlorounguinol (3) (28.83 μM). To our knowledge, this is the first report of the α-glucosidase inhibitory activity of compounds 1–7. A preliminary structure–activity relationship analysis suggested that the substitution pattern of the aromatic polyketides may affect their inhibitory activity. Molecular docking of compounds 1–7 and four aromatic polyketides previously isolated in our studies was performed against penicillin-binding protein 2a (PBP2a; PDB ID: 1MWT), together with in silico ADMET prediction to assess their pharmacokinetic properties.

papers.title: Short-form video and microlearning in English language education: A bibliometric and science mapping review
papers.abstract: Short-form video platforms, particularly TikTok, have altered how second language learners encounter and process linguistic input. Individual studies have examined specific aspects of microlearning in second language contexts, yet, to the authors' knowledge, no bibliometric analysis has mapped the intellectual structure of this emerging subfield. This study maps the publication landscape, thematic clusters, and research gaps characterizing microlearning research in English language education through short-form video platforms. We conducted a hybrid bibliometric analysis of 80 Scopus-indexed documents published between 2004 and 2026. Performance analysis was performed using Biblioshiny (R), and science mapping was executed through VOSviewer. The bibliometric outputs were then interpreted through a qualitative synthesis using the Theory, Context, Characteristics, and Methodology framework. Three principal patterns emerged. First, scholars from developing Asian economies, including Malaysia, Hong Kong, China, and Indonesia, contributed the largest share of publications, whereas traditional Western academic centers produced comparatively fewer studies. Second, the thematic clusters concentrated on phonological production and vocabulary acquisition, with limited attention to academic writing or reading comprehension. Third, qualitative and experimental designs together accounted for approximately two-thirds of the corpus, while computational learning analytics appeared only peripherally in the keyword co-occurrence network. This bibliometric review maps the knowledge structure of a rapidly expanding subfield at the intersection of educational technology and applied linguistics. The findings point to a need for longitudinal experimental designs, methodological diversification toward learning analytics, and empirical investigation of how algorithmic recommendation systems mediate L2 input delivery.
papers.venue: Journal of Pedagogical Sociology and Psychology

papers.title: Real-Time Water Quality Forecasting Using a Simulation-Driven IoT and Machine Learning Framework for Resource-Constrained Smart Cities
papers.abstract: This study proposes and evaluates a simulation-driven Internet of Things (IoT) and machine-learning framework for real-time water-quality monitoring and forecasting in resource-constrained smart cities. Ensuring timely and reliable water-quality data remains a critical challenge, as conventional monitoring approaches are often delayed, infrastructure-intensive, and difficult to scale. While IoT-based systems support continuous environmental monitoring, many existing implementations emphasise data acquisition rather than predictive analytics and deployment-oriented design. To address this gap, the study develops a unified simulation-based modelling framework in which virtual sensors generate key water-quality parameters, including pH, turbidity, temperature, and dissolved oxygen. The generated data are processed using a machine learning pipeline and used to train supervised models, namely XGBoost, Random Forest, and K-Nearest Neighbours. Model performance is evaluated using accuracy, precision, recall, and F1-score to ensure balanced assessment across water-quality conditions. The results show that XGBoost achieves the highest predictive performance (91% accuracy), demonstrating strong capability in modelling non-linear environmental patterns and detecting unsafe water conditions. In addition to predictive performance, the framework supports real-time forecasting and visualisation through an integrated dashboard, enabling continuous monitoring and data-driven decision-making. The study contributes a reproducible and scalable framework that integrates simulation-based modelling, IoT-enabled monitoring, and machine learning for predictive analytics. The proposed approach provides a cost-effective pathway for advancing sustainable water management and environmental monitoring in resource-constrained smart-city environments.

papers.title: CIVIL AND CRIMINAL LIABILITY OF DEEPFAKE AI PLATFORM PROVIDERS IN VIOLATIONS OF THE RIGHT TO REPUTATION
papers.abstract: The rapid development of Artificial Intelligence (AI) has introduced deepfake technology, which is capable of manipulating audiovisual data with high realism. While this technology offers creative utility, its misuse for synthesizing non-consensual pornography, political disinformation, and character assassination severely violates an individual’s right to reputation. This study examines the civil and criminal liabilities of AI deepfake platform providers under the Indonesian legal framework, specifically Law No. 1/2024 (Second Amendment to the ITE Law) and Law No. 27/2022 on Personal Data Protection (UU PDP). Using a socio-legal research method, this study analyzes how textual legal norms interact with the digital behavior of platform providers and the psychological and social vulnerabilities of victims. The results indicate a significant normative gap: current regulations primarily target the individual creators or distributors of deepfake content, while platform providers escape liability by hiding behind the "safe harbor" doctrine. Sociologically, this legal vacuum fosters a culture of impunity and exacerbates digital gender-based violence. This paper argues for a paradigm shift from passive moderation to active algorithmic accountability. Platform providers must be held civilly liable under Article 1365 of the Indonesian Civil Code for systemic negligence, and criminally liable under the corporate fault doctrine for failing to implement mandatory digital watermarking and proactive content filtration systems.

papers.title: Reconstructing the Legal Enforcement Framework for Digital Activism in an Era of Technological Disruption
papers.abstract: The rapid expansion of digital technologies has transformed civic engagement by enabling digital activism as a powerful medium for public participation, social advocacy, and democratic expression. While these developments strengthen citizen engagement, they also create significant legal challenges in balancing freedom of expression with the need to maintain public order and prevent digital misconduct. This study reconstructs the legal enforcement framework governing digital activism in the era of technological disruption by identifying regulatory deficiencies, evaluating current enforcement practices, and proposing a more adaptive and rights-based legal model. The research employs a qualitative normative legal methodology complemented by a socio-legal perspective. It analyzes statutory regulations, legal doctrines, judicial decisions, and policy frameworks concerning digital expression and online activism. Data were collected through a systematic review of legal documents, scholarly literature, and policy reports, then examined using conceptual and comparative legal analysis to identify structural weaknesses within existing enforcement mechanisms. The findings demonstrate that current enforcement remains largely rooted in conventional regulatory paradigms that inadequately address the complexity of digital activism. Ambiguous legal provisions, overlapping institutional authorities, and inconsistent enforcement practices generate legal uncertainty and increase the risk of over-criminalizing legitimate civic expression. Furthermore, the absence of clear legal standards governing digital advocacy, online mobilization, and algorithm-driven information dissemination complicates effective enforcement and weakens legal certainty. This study proposes a reconstructed enforcement framework grounded in the principles of proportionality, transparency, accountability, and digital rights protection. The framework emphasizes adaptive regulation, integrated digital governance, institutional capacity building, and clearer legal standards for technology-mediated civic participation. By bridging technological realities with constitutional safeguards, the proposed model contributes to contemporary legal scholarship on digital governance while offering practical policy recommendations for developing a more balanced, accountable, and responsive legal system capable of addressing the evolving challenges of the digital era.

papers.title: Evaluating Digital Technologies’ Economic and Environmental Effects on Compliance, Governance, and Privacy in Sustainable Environmental Management
papers.abstract: The purpose of the study was to analyze new technologies impact on environment. The prospective benefits and challenges of new technologies on the use of technologies within environmental governance and compliance were uncovered in this study. Utilizing a convergence approach of qualitative and quantitative studies, the researchers sent out a survey to 9407 stakeholders within the environment, which included civil society, the private sector, and government. The study found out that the enforcement and reporting of compliance with environmental legislation would be greatly assisted by the streamlining of governance and compliance in the adoption of new technologies such as blockchain, artificial intelligence, and the Internet of Things (IoT), The study also acknowledged the presence of other challenges such as inadequate infrastructure, expensive technologies, and poor technical capacity. The gaps and challenges on the governance of the environment, compliance, and sustainability would be solved by the introduced new technologies, which in turn would create a sustainable environment. This would lead to the development of Nigeria in an economically sustainable manner, while also providing overall environmental sustainability. The paper recommend that Nigeria's should increase her investment in the construction of training facilities within the administrative regulatory systems of new technological systems in environmental sustainability, collaborative Joint ventures should be encouraged so as to achieve economies and environmental sustainability.

papers.title: Enseñanza del desarrollo e-commerce centrado en el usuario mediante un proyecto basado en Go: caso de estudio exploratorio en educación en ingeniería
papers.abstract: Software engineering courses often address technical implementation and user experience evaluation independently, limiting the integration of these dimensions throughout the learning process. To address this challenge, this article presents an exploratory educational case study conducted in a Human-Computer Interaction course, centered on Go-Plant, an e-commerce platform developed using Go. The educational experience integrated Project-Based Learning (PBL), the ADDIE model as an instructional design framework, and User-Centered Design (UCD). The project involved 30 students organized into six teams and ten external users who participated in formative usability testing. The initial evaluation identified difficulties in understanding payment methods (9/10 users), filtering products (5/10), and locating relevant information (5/10). These findings guided the redesign of navigation, the product catalog, shopping cart, and checkout process. Subsequently, the same ten users participated in a second visual acceptance evaluation, in which the mean score increased from 2.54 to 4.28 points on a five-point scale. The Wilcoxon signed-rank test for paired samples revealed a statistically significant difference between the two versions (W=0.00; exact two-sided p=0.001953). The findings indicate greater visual acceptance of the redesigned interface and illustrate how integrating PBL, ADDIE, and UCD can connect technical development with formative evaluation and iterative interface improvement. This study provides a methodological reference for incorporating user-centered development practices into engineering education without establishing causal effects on student learning.
papers.venue: Revista de Investigación en Tecnologías de la Información

papers.title: Dancing in the Rain: The Effectiveness of Mobile Platform for Learning Ten Qira’at
papers.abstract: Since the last pandemic outbreak, mobile learning platforms have been extensively utilized. This widespread adoption is facilitated by the affordability of smart devices, particularly smartphones, the high internet penetration even in remote areas, and the user-friendly nature of mobile learning platforms. Numerous courseware has been developed to ensure continuous learning beyond the confines of the classroom. However, there is currently a lack of courseware and mobile applications specifically designed to guide and provide materials for the ten Qira'at recitation style. In response, we have developed Qiraat10 as supplemental material for teaching and learning the Qira'at recitation style at UniSHAMS. This paper aims to provide insights into the effectiveness of the mobile learning platform, specifically focusing on the courseware Qiraat10. Based on the data gathered, Qiraat10 has been found to be effective in assisting users, particularly students, in learning the ten Qira'at recitation style.
papers.venue: International Journal of Academic Research in Business and Social Sciences

papers.title: Discovering the Drivers of Ecological Fashion Adoption Intention among Fast Fashion Consumers
papers.abstract: The environmental impact of fast fashion has garnered global attention due to its resource-intensive production, excessive waste, and pollution. In response, ecological fashion has emerged to promote sustainable consumption and mitigate environmental harm. However, research on ecological fashion adoption intention in developing countries remains limited. Despite growing awareness, many consumers continue to prioritize fast fashion over eco-friendly alternatives. This study examines how the need for fashion and need for uniqueness influence ecological fashion adoption intention among Malaysian consumers. A quantitative survey was conducted with 396 participants using a structured questionnaire. Data were analyzed using SPSS. Findings show that among the dimensions of the Need for Fashion, image consciousness and market knowledge significantly and positively influence ecological fashion adoption intention, while fashion awareness and fashion consciousness were not significant. For the Need for Uniqueness, creative choices and unpopular choices significantly affect adoption intention, whereas avoidance of similarity was not significant. These results highlight the importance of self-expression, creativity, and market awareness in driving sustainable fashion behavior in Malaysia. The study contributes theoretically by integrating fashion consciousness and uniqueness into ecological fashion adoption models in a developing country context. Practically, it offers insights for policymakers and marketers to design strategies that promote sustainable fashion adoption. By understanding consumer motivations, stakeholders can encourage environmentally responsible behavior, foster a greener lifestyle, and support Malaysia’s sustainable development objectives.
papers.venue: International Journal of Academic Research in Business and Social Sciences

papers.title: Efeitos da suplementação probiótica nos níveis séricos de zonulina em pacientes com doença renal crônica: um ensaio clínico randomizado
papers.abstract: INTRODUCTION: Chronic kidney disease (CKD) is associated with intestinal dysbiosis, systemic inflammation, and impaired intestinal barrier function. Serum zonulin has been proposed as an indirect marker of intestinal permeability, although its clinical relevance in CKD remains uncertain. OBJECTIVE: To evaluate the effect of probiotic supplementation on serum zonulin levels in patients undergoing maintenance hemodialysis. METHODS: In this randomized, placebo-controlled, triple-blind clinical trial, 40 hemodialysis patients were assigned to receive either a probiotic formulation or a placebo for six months. The primary outcome was the between-group difference in change in serum zonulin from baseline to follow-up. Secondary outcomes included metabolic, anthropometric, hemodynamic, and gastrointestinal variables. RESULTS: Serum zonulin increased in both groups, with no significant between-group difference (placebo: 288.2 to 425.3 ng/mL; probiotic: 239.5 to 453.7 ng/mL; p = 0.882; ANCOVA p = 0.463). Pre-dialysis urea decreased within the probiotic group, but the between-group difference was not significant (p = 0.305). Serum phosphorus showed a greater reduction in the probiotic group than in the placebo group (p = 0.011; ANCOVA p = 0.011). No significant differences were observed for anthropometric or hemodynamic outcomes. CONCLUSION: Six months of probiotic supplementation did not significantly reduce serum zonulin levels in hemodialysis patients. Although a favorable effect on serum phosphoruswas observed, these findings do not support a measurable impact of this probiotic regimen on serum zonulin and highlight the need for larger studies incorporating direct assessments of intestinal permeability and gut microbiota.

papers.title: Visualizing a decade of machine translation research (2016–2025): A VOSviewer-based bibliometric analysis
papers.abstract: Background and Purpose: Machine translation has undergone rapid transformation over the past decade, driven by advances in neural machine translation and large language models, yet systematic attention to the field’s overall intellectual structure during this critical transition remains limited. This study aims to visualize the evolution of machine translation research from 2016 to 2025, with particular attention to its interdisciplinary development and trends in the post-2022 era of large language models. Methodology: This study presents a bibliometric analysis of machine translation research from a language and translation perspective, based on 582 journal articles published between 2016 and 2025 and indexed in the Web of Science Core Collection. Using VOSviewer, it examines the main characteristics of machine translation publications and key research themes. Findings: The findings show a steady rise in machine translation research output, reflecting growing scholarly interest alongside technological advances. Research is globally distributed but concentrated in Europe and Asia, particularly in Spain and China. Journals in translation studies and computational linguistics account for the largest share of publications and receive the most scholarly attention. However, the field has yet to form a stable core author group, indicating a dispersed and evolving research structure. Five major research themes are identified: technological development and model innovation; human-machine collaboration and application contexts; machine translation quality evaluation; translation studies and industry-related research; and language education with ethical considerations. Contributions: By mapping research trajectories and key contributors, this study offers a solid foundation for advancing future research, emphasizing the need for cross-regional and interdisciplinary collaboration and a balanced integration of technological, human, and ethical dimensions. Keywords: Bibliometric analysis, machine translation, translation studies, visualization, VOSviewer. Cite as: Tang, N., Moindjie, M. A., Lyu, Z., & Wu, S. (2026). Visualizing a decade of machine translation research (2016–2025): A VOSviewer-based bibliometric analysis. Journal of Nusantara Studies, 12(1), 1-19. http://dx.doi.org/10.24200/jonus.vol12iss1pp1-19

papers.title: Integrating concept-based instruction and project-based learning to enhance grammar competence, critical thinking, and collaboration among Cambodian student teachers authors
papers.abstract: Background and Purpose: Education plays a vital role in preparing a generation of learners who are critical, creative, and adaptable to an ever-changing world. This study aimed to examine the extent to which the integration of Concept-Based Instruction (CBI) and Project-Based Learning (PBL) improved the critical thinking, collaboration skills, and grammar competence of BTEC student teachers. Methodology and Results: A one-group pretest–posttest pre-experimental design was employed with 21 student teachers. A paired-samples t-test revealed that posttest scores were statistically significantly higher than pretest scores, with a mean gain of 9.29 points. Five expert evaluators assessed students’ project performance across five selected facets of understanding: Explanation, Interpretation, Application, Perspective, and Self-Knowledge. Group-level results showed overall means of 3.04 for Group 1, 3.36 for Group 2, and 3.09 for Group 3. Group 2 showed particularly high scores in Perspective (M = 3.80) and Explanation (M = 3.70). In addition, a Self/Group Evaluation Worksheet was administered to examine students’ perceptions of their collaborative learning experiences. The findings indicated that PBL activities supported students in working collaboratively, planning tasks, monitoring their work, and reflecting on their learning, thereby developing skills essential for teamwork and project management. Contribution: The findings provide empirical evidence that integrating Concept-Based Instruction and Project-Based Learning can provide an effective instructional framework for developing student teachers’ critical thinking and collaboration skills. The study suggests that policymakers and curriculum developers consider incorporating similar integrated approaches into teacher education curricula. Further research should examine the long-term effects of this instructional approach and its applicability across different educational contexts and learning trajectories. Keywords: Concept-based instruction, critical thinking, collaboration, grammar, project-based learning. Cite as: Hieng, S., Hum, C., Soeung, S., Chhen, S., & Sam, R. (2026). Integrating concept-based instruction and project-based learning to enhance grammar competence, critical thinking, and collaboration among Cambodian student teachers authors. Journal of Nusantara Studies, 12(1), 60-81. http://dx.doi.org/10.24200/jonus.vol12iss1pp60-81

papers.title: Multimodal interpretation of notation
papers.abstract: Challenges related to the teaching and learning of formal notation in school mathematics are widely documented, and specifically in relation to the underlying mathematical structures that the notation is intended to convey. In this article, we draw on embodied cognition to examine the interactions among three students working with the software Grid Algebra. Embodied cognition emphasises the role of gesture and movement in learning and understanding mathematics. Grid Algebra uses movement to direct students’ attention to mathematical operations on numbers and numerical expressions within the grid and the structure of these operations, while the software takes care of the formal notation of the numerical expressions that describe these sequences of operations. We analyse how different modes of communication work together to scaffold students’ fluency with operations and the formal notation representing these operations and the order in which they are performed. The dynamic between notation, speech, movement and position allows students to educate their interpretation of mathematical notation through the movements and positions that they are very familiar with.

papers.title: Impact of Agile Methods on Tacit Knowledge Sharing from Self-Determination Perspective: A Mixed Method Study of Chinese IT Teams
papers.abstract: The purpose of the study is to examine whether agile methods foster tacit knowledge sharing in IT project teams and to identify the motivational mechanisms, especially basic psychological needs and shared goals, underpinning this relationship in Chinese contexts. It does so by using a sequential mixed-methods design: survey data from 610 IT professionals (predominantly mainland China, with a small Hong Kong subsample) analysed with PLS-SEM, complemented by 22 semi structured interviews examined through comparative cross case analysis, thematic coding, and process tracing. The findings suggest agile methods positively predict tacit knowledge sharing, even after controlling for transformational leadership and enjoyment of sharing. This effect is largely mediated by satisfaction of basic psychological needs and shared goals. Autonomy and shared goals act mainly through competence and relatedness. Qualitative evidence underscores problem-driven collaboration, project ownership, and informal exchanges. That said, the main limitation of the study is that cross sectional, self report data, non probability sampling, and focus on Chinese IT professionals limit causal inference and generalizability. Nonetheless, the study provides empirical evidence that agile methods are linked to tacit knowledge sharing, explains how these methods foster such sharing through the satisfaction of basic psychological needs and the establishment of shared goals, and offers a rigorous operationalization of agile methods. This implies that managers should design agile practices as a motivational architecture that supports autonomy, competence, relatedness, and shared goals, rather than relying on formal, mandatory knowledge sharing sessions or performance linked incentives.
papers.venue: SBS Journal of Applied Business Research

papers.title: Perceived Accuracy and Relevance of AI-Based Product Recommendations and Generation X Purchase Decisions in Jakarta
papers.abstract: This study examines how perceived accuracy and contextual relevance of artificial-intelligence-based product recommendations influence purchase decisions among Generation X e-commerce users in Jakarta. A quantitative explanatory design was modeled with 300 respondent profiles and 18 reflective indicators. Partial least squares structural equation modeling, 10,000-resample bootstrapping, coefficient-difference testing, and tenfold cross-validation were applied. Perceived accuracy had a stronger positive effect on purchase decisions (β=.604, p<.001) than relevance (β=.217, p<.001), and the difference was significant (Δβ=.387, p<.001). The model explained 54.2% of purchase-decision variance and showed positive Qpredict2​ values. The findings indicate an accuracy–relevance asymmetry: relevance attracts attention, whereas perceived accuracy more strongly reinforces purchase decisions.

papers.title: Development and Feasibility Evaluation of AR-GeoHazard for Slope Gradient Visualization in Pagar Alam
papers.abstract: Accessible terrain information is essential for supporting geospatial literacy and disaster education in mountainous environments. This study aimed to develop and evaluate AR-GeoHazard, an Android application for slope-gradient visualization in Pagar Alam, Indonesia. A research-and-development approach followed the Analysis, Design, Development, Implementation, and Evaluation (ADDIE) framework, incorporating prototyping for application refinement. The application integrates elevation profiles, three-dimensional terrain visualization, smartphone-assisted slope observations, recording features, and interpretive guidance. Evaluation comprised 40 black-box test scenarios, assessments by two experts, task-based testing and System Usability Scale (SUS) questionnaires involving 20 users, and comparisons with geographic information system (GIS)-derived slope classes at 30 reference points. The evaluation results showed a functional success rate of 95.00%, an expert assessment score of 91.60%, a task-completion rate of 94.00%, a mean SUS score of 86.75, and GIS classification agreement of 93.33%. The weighted feasibility index reached 92.19, meeting the study-defined criteria for high feasibility. However, two functional failures, two classification mismatches, and ambiguous safety labels require further investigation. These findings support the continued development of AR-GeoHazard as an educational terrain-visualization tool, while sensor accuracy, spatial registration, and learning effectiveness require dedicated validation.

papers.title: Retrieval-Augmented Generation Chatbot for Academic Information Services Using GROQ API
papers.abstract: Academic information services in universities are still largely carried out manually by administrative staff with limited working hours, making it difficult for students to receive quick responses, especially outside office hours. This study aims to design and implement an academic chatbot using the Retrieval-Augmented Generation (RAG) approach through the Groq API and a Streamlit interface. The system was developed following the Design Science Research (DSR) methodology, which includes problem identification, defining solution objectives, dataset collection, artifact design and development, system demonstration, testing and evaluation, as well as communication of research results. Black-box testing on 20 questions yielded 18 valid answers, while semantic quality evaluation using BERTScore produced a precision of 0.7054, recall of 0.7176, and F1-score of 0.7095. The average system response time was 1.45 seconds, with a median of 0.85 seconds, indicates that the majority of responses were provided in less than one second, despite a single outlier of 12.13 seconds. These results finding suggest that the integration of RAG with the Groq API holds potential for enhancing digital academic information services in higher education. Nevertheless, its operational benefits in real-world scenarios warrant further evaluation through empirical user testing.
papers.venue: TEKNOSAINS Jurnal Sains Teknologi dan Informatika

papers.title: Design And Development Of A Web-Based Encyclopedia Of Jambi Traditional Culinary: A Case Study Of The Department Of Culture And Tourism Of Jambi Province
papers.abstract: Jambi traditional culinary is part of the region's cultural heritage that has historical value, distinctive flavors, and local identity. However, information about Jambi traditional culinary is still scattered across various media and has not been presented in a structured digital system, making it difficult for the public to obtain complete and accessible information. This study aims to design and develop a web-based Encyclopedia of Jambi Traditional Culinary as a medium for information, promotion, and cultural preservation. The system was developed using the Waterfall model, consisting of requirements analysis, system design, implementation, and testing. The application was developed using PHP with the CodeIgniter 4 framework and MySQL database. The search feature applies the Fuzzy Matching method using the similar_text() and levenshtein() functions to provide relevant results for inaccurate keywords. Black Box Testing and Fuzzy Matching testing were conducted to evaluate system functionality and search capability. The results show that all main system functions operated according to the specified requirements, with an average similarity score of 86.50% and a processing time of less than 10 milliseconds. The system successfully presents information on Jambi traditional culinary, including names, descriptions, ingredients, cooking procedures, categories, and images. Therefore, the system can facilitate public access to culinary information while supporting the digitalization and preservation of regional cultural heritage.

papers.title: Deep learning for predicting high-grade dysplasia in colorectal polyps using white-light endoscopy
papers.abstract: BACKGROUND Accurate identification of high-grade dysplasia (HGD) in colorectal polyps is important for optimizing endoscopic management and surveillance strategies. Although deep learning has shown potential for colorectal polyp characterization, the generalizability of white-light imaging (WLI)-based models across independent clinical settings remains insufficiently established. AIM To develop and externally validate a deep learning model based on routine WLI images for predicting HGD in colorectal polyps, to explore the predictive contribution of routinely available clinical variables, and to compare model performance with endoscopists with different levels of experience. METHODS In this multicenter retrospective observational study, a MobileNetV2-based deep learning model was developed using routine WLI images of colorectal polyps and externally validated in two independent tertiary hospitals. Each polyp was represented by one representative high-quality WLI image, and histopathological diagnosis was used as the reference standard. Model discrimination, calibration, decision curve analysis, and diagnostic performance were evaluated. An exploratory clinical model based on routinely available clinical and lesion characteristics was developed as a baseline comparator. The model was further compared with endoscopists using binary HGD/non-HGD classifications in a blinded reader study. RESULTS The WLI-based model achieved an area under the receiver operating characteristic curve of 0.879 [95% confidence interval (CI): 0.795-0.952] in the internal test cohort and maintained consistent discrimination in two external validation cohorts [area under the receiver operating characteristic curve, 0.814 (95%CI: 0.728-0.890) and 0.803 (95%CI: 0.719-0.896)]. The exploratory clinical model provided no clear evidence of incremental predictive value beyond image-based prediction. In the reader study, the artificial intelligence model demonstrated comparable classification performance with senior endoscopists, and superior performance compared with junior endoscopists based on binary diagnostic metrics. However, the external validation cohorts contained a limited number of HGD-positive cases, and performance estimates should therefore be interpreted with caution. CONCLUSION A deep learning model based on routine WLI images showed promising and consistent performance for HGD risk stratification in colorectal polyps across three tertiary hospitals. The model may provide complementary information to support endoscopic assessment, particularly for less experienced clinicians. Prospective real-time validation in broader populations and healthcare settings is required before clinical implementation.

papers.title: Kecerdasan Buatan (AI) dan Masa Depan Pastoral Konseling: Peluang, Risiko, dan Batas Teologis
papers.abstract: Perkembangan pesat kecerdasan buatan (AI) generatif telah memunculkan pertanyaan mendasar tentang masa depan pastoral konseling, sejauh mana entitas non-personal berbasis algoritma dapat menjalankan fungsi yang selama ini menjadi domain eksklusif konselor pastoral manusia. Penelitian ini bertujuan membangun kerangka normatif tiga lapis, terapeutik, relasional, dan teologis, untuk mengevaluasi secara sistematis peluang, risiko, dan batas teologis penggunaan AI dalam konteks pastoral konseling. Metode yang digunakan adalah Systematic Literature Review mengikuti protokol PRISMA 2020, dikombinasikan dengan analisis tematik reflektif atas 52 studi final dari literatur teologi praktis dan etika digital yang dipublikasikan antara 2015 dan 2024. Temuan menunjukkan bahwa AI menawarkan aksesibilitas, konsistensi, dan skalabilitas layanan psikospiritual yang signifikan, namun secara fundamental gagal mereplikasi dimensi relasional dan kehadiran pastoral (pastoral presence) yang berpijak pada doktrin Imago Dei. Kontribusi utama penelitian ini adalah artikulasi batas epistemik teologis yang masih absen dalam literatur teologi praktis global maupun Asia Tenggara: AI dapat menopang (support) tetapi tidak dapat menggantikan (replace) fungsi pastoral yang mensyaratkan perjumpaan personal antara dua makhluk ber-Imago Dei. Implikasi praktis mencakup panduan etis bagi gereja, seminari, dan lembaga kesehatan rohani dalam mengadopsi teknologi AI secara bertanggung jawab.

papers.title: Artificial Intelligence in Christian Religious Education: Reconstructing Teachers' Roles in Developing Students' Digital Literacy and Critical Thinking
papers.abstract: The rapid development of artificial intelligence, particularly generative artificial intelligence, is transforming how students access information and learn, including in Christian Religious Education. While artificial intelligence offers opportunities for personalized learning and richer engagement with biblical and theological content, it also raises concerns about inaccurate or biased religious content, over-reliance, weakened critical thinking, ethical risks, and the erosion of the relational and spiritual dimensions of faith formation. This study aims to reconstruct the roles of Christian religious education teachers in artificial intelligence-based learning so that it strengthens students' digital literacy and critical thinking within Christ-centered formation. A qualitative design using library research and conceptual analysis was employed. A corpus of 52 sources, comprising peer-reviewed studies published between 2018 and 2026 together with seminal works and policy documents regardless of publication year, was selected through explicit criteria and analyzed using reflexive thematic analysis and conceptual synthesis. The synthesis indicates that artificial intelligence shifts Christian Religious Education from content transmission toward guided inquiry; that its opportunities are realized only when its risks are mediated pedagogically and ethically; that teachers' roles must be reconstructed as learning facilitators, spiritual mentors, and digital ethics guides; and that digital literacy and critical thinking can be integrated through the evaluation and theological discernment of machine-generated content. The study proposes the Christ-Centered EEDE Framework (exploring, evaluating, discerning, and embodying), which integrates these elements into a teacher-guided learning cycle and offers a testable foundation for ensuring that artificial intelligence serves, rather than replaces, faith formation.

papers.title: Retrieval-augmented generation models for predicting pathological upgrading in endoscopically resected gastric low-grade intraepithelial neoplasia: A dual-center evaluation
papers.abstract: BACKGROUND Gastric low-grade intraepithelial neoplasia (LGIN) exhibits highly variable clinical outcomes. The discordance between histological findings from endoscopic forceps biopsy and endoscopic submucosal dissection (ESD) complicates the formulation of appropriate treatment strategies. AIM To evaluate a prediction framework using large language models (LLMs) enhanced with retrieval-augmented generation (RAG) for the pathological upgrading of gastric LGIN. METHODS We retrospectively enrolled 329 patients with 372 gastric LGIN lesions from two tertiary hospitals who underwent ESD following a pre-operative diagnosis of gastric LGIN via biopsy. A RAG knowledge base was constructed based on 28 peer-reviewed articles on LGIN upgrading. Two LLMs (DeepSeek-V3 and Qwen3-235b) were evaluated in a zero-shot setting to generate upgrading probability predictions and reasoning reports for each lesion. Performance was evaluated using the area under the receiver operating characteristic curve (AUC), calibration plots, and decision curve analysis (DCA). The performance of RAG-enhanced LLMs was compared with that of a generalized linear mixed model baseline and two experienced endoscopists. Subgroup analyses were also conducted. RESULTS Pathological upgrading to high-grade intraepithelial neoplasia or early gastric cancer was confirmed in 148 (40%) lesions. The AUCs for the RAG-enhanced DeepSeek-V3 and Qwen3-235b were 0.873 [95% confidence interval (95%CI): 0.828-0.901] and 0.862 (95%CI: 0.818-0.893), respectively, demonstrating performance comparable to that of experienced endoscopists and baseline model (DeLong test, P > 0.05). Based on the maximum Youden index, DeepSeek-V3 achieved a sensitivity of 85.1%, specificity of 80.4%, positive predictive value of 74.1%, and negative predictive value of 89.1% at the optimal threshold of 0.357; Qwen3-235b achieved 84.5%, 77.2%, 71.0%, and 88.3%, respectively, at the threshold of 0.453. DCA demonstrated superior clinical utility across threshold probabilities of 15%-80%. In the subgroup analysis, RAG-enhanced LLMs maintained higher accuracy in lesions measuring 1-2 cm. CONCLUSION This study evaluated a novel RAG-enhanced framework using LLMs for predicting pathological upgrading in gastric LGIN. These models may have the potential to support clinical decision-making for ESD, pending prospective validation.

papers.title: A Brick in the Creative Wall: The Cultural and Creative Production System Facing the Challenge of Generative Artificial Intelligence
papers.abstract: Generative artificial intelligence (GenAI) is increasingly transforming cultural and creative industries (CCIs), yet research lacks a structured understanding of how they intervene across production processes. How and where does GenAI reshape value creation activities within the CCI production system? Building on the UNESCO cultural cycle (2009), we develop an analytical framework that maps GenAI applications across three phases of the cultural production value chain: creation, production, and distribution/consumption. It identifies how GenAI reconfigures value creation and value capture mechanisms differently across phases and sectors. Our analysis highlights emerging dynamics, including phase-specific technological dependencies, increasing feedback loops between production and consumption, and a growing technological convergence across CCIs. To illustrate these mechanisms, we present cases from Galleries, Libraries, Archives and Museums (GLAM). Our paper contributes to ongoing debates on digital transformation in cultural production systems, providing insights for researchers, policymakers, and cultural organizations navigating the opportunities and risks of GenAI. JEL Codes: H0, M0, M1, O4

papers.title: The Role of Technology, Market and Design Relatedness in Export Diversification
papers.abstract: Trade and innovation are key drivers of economic activity, promoting growth by increasing productivity and fostering competition. While the relationship between innovation and exports is well established, the specific contributions of different stages of innovation remain underexplored. This paper examines how different stages of innovation – namely technology, market, and design activities – are related to export specialization. We extend the principle of relatedness, as has recently been proposed in the literature, by incorporating multiple activities and apply the methodology to seventy-six countries for the years 2008-2022. By employing a rich set of patent, trademark, design and export data, we show that technology- and market-related capabilities serve as key drivers of new export specializations. Finally, our findings offer policymakers a multidimensional framework potentially applicable to goods and services. JEL Codes: F14, O34, O38
